title: Quick-chat endpoint cannot be used to fish another project's indexed documents (MRB-03)
description: Regression guard: before the MRB-03 fix, POST /chat/quick forwarded a client-supplied projectId straight to the Python RAG backend with no membership verification, letting any org member read another project's indexed evidence/policy corpus through the stateless quick-chat path.
preconditions: Caller is a member of Project A only
Project B in the same org has indexed evidence documents
steps: As the Project-A-only user, POST /api/assistant/chat/quick with { message: 'summarize evidence', projectId: <Project B id> }
expectedResult: 403 ProjectAccessDeniedError before any call reaches the RAG backend. No fragment of Project B's document corpus appears in the response body.

title: A follow-up chat message cannot redirect an existing conversation's RAG retrieval to a foreign project
description: chat.routes.ts always re-derives projectId from the stored conversation record for an existing thread — a client-supplied projectId in the follow-up request body is read but discarded. Verifies this cannot be bypassed by also supplying the foreign projectId inside context.projectId.
preconditions: An existing conversation was created scoped to Project A
Caller also belongs to Project B
steps: POST /api/assistant/chat with { conversationId: <projA-conv>, message: 'x', projectId: <projB-id>, context: { projectId: <projB-id> } }
expectedResult: org_context.project_id forwarded to the Python backend is Project A's id in all cases — neither the top-level nor context.projectId override succeeds.

title: A conversationId belonging to another user cannot be read, extended, or have its messages listed
description: getConversation()'s Mongo filter requires userId equality (or a legacy record with no userId), closing the org-scoped-only gap where any member could pass a guessed/leaked conversation ObjectId belonging to a colleague.
preconditions: User A owns conversation C with several messages
User B is a different member of the same org and knows C's id
steps: As User B: POST /api/assistant/chat with conversationId=C_id
expectedResult: All three requests return 404 for User B. No message content, title, or metadata belonging to User A's conversation is disclosed.

title: Hardcoded DEV_FALLBACK_TOKEN in aiAssistantService.js must never be a valid, accepted token outside local development
description: aiAssistantService.js ships a hardcoded HS256 JWT fallback (DEV_FALLBACK_TOKEN) used whenever no NextAuth session token exists in development/DEV_MODE. Because it is a plain string literal committed to the client bundle, it is trivially extractable by anyone who loads the app's JS. If the gateway's Keycloak validation ever falls back to accepting an unsigned/dev-mode path in staging or production, this becomes a static, universally-known bearer credential.
preconditions: Access to a staging or production build of vibrantix-client-panel
steps: Extract DEV_FALLBACK_TOKEN from the shipped client bundle (it is a literal string, not env-injected)
Send it as 'Authorization: Bearer <token>' directly to the staging/production assistant-service /api/assistant/chat endpoint
expectedResult: The gateway's Keycloak plugin rejects the token in any non-local environment (invalid signature / not issued by the real Keycloak realm) — 401. If it is ever accepted, this is a critical finding: a hardcoded, publicly-extractable token granting AI assistant access.

title: Structured audit logging for AI Assistant requests records the HTTP transaction but not the AI-generated content, tools invoked, or route taken
description: structured-logging.ts's onResponse hook writes an audit entry (action, resource='ai_assistant', outcome) for any URL containing '/assistant/', but the entry contains no reference to aiResponse.content, tools_used, or route_path — the fields chat.routes.ts already receives from the Python backend. Per ISO 27001 Annex A.8.16 (Monitoring Activities), detecting AI-generated content misuse requires visibility into what the model actually said and which tools it invoked, not just that a 200 was returned.
preconditions: Access to assistant-service's audit log output
steps: Send a chat message that triggers a tool call and produces a substantive AI answer
Inspect the emitted audit log entry for that request
expectedResult: Current behavior: the audit entry shows { action: 'POST /api/assistant/chat', resource: 'ai_assistant', outcome: 'success' } with no route_path, tools_used, or content reference — insufficient on its own to reconstruct or flag misuse of AI-generated output after the fact. Flag as a gap against A.8.16 monitoring intent; remediation is to include route_path/tools_used (not full content, to avoid over-retention of user data) in the audit entry.

title: Evidence citation display renders source/type/summary with no clickable link back to the underlying evidence, so link-target correctness cannot be verified end-to-end
description: RAGResponseMetadata.jsx's EvidenceCitations component renders evidence.source/type/summary as inert badges/text; it never reads or renders evidence.url (present on SourceReference/EvidenceReference in the backend types) as a link, and GRCChatPage's citation badges likewise render `c.source || c` with no onClick/href. A user cannot click a citation to open the corresponding evidence or policy file — meaning there is currently no click-through path whose target-correctness could even be verified.
preconditions: A chat response includes citations/evidenceRefs with a populated url field
steps: Trigger a response that returns citations with source.url pointing at a real evidence item
Attempt to click the rendered citation in the chat UI
expectedResult: Current behavior: the citation renders as plain text/badge with no click affordance and no navigation occurs — flag as a functional gap. If/when a click-through is implemented, this case should be re-run to confirm it opens the evidence belonging to the citing organization only (never a cross-tenant document).

title: Redis-backed rate limiter fails OPEN on a Redis error, temporarily removing the AI-cost protection
description: RateLimiter.checkRedisLimit() explicitly catches any Redis error and returns { allowed: true, remaining: limit } ('Fail open - allow request on Redis error'). During a Redis outage this silently disables the global/per-org/per-user/aiQuery rate limits (rate-limit.ts), leaving only the route-level in-memory-fallback limiter on /chat itself as protection against runaway LLM spend.
preconditions: Ability to simulate Redis unavailability in a test environment
steps: Simulate a Redis connection failure (e.g. block the REDIS_URL port)
Exceed the normal perUser (50/min) or aiQuery (20/min) limit while Redis is down
expectedResult: Requests are NOT rejected with 429 while Redis is unreachable — confirms the documented fail-open behavior. This is a deliberate availability-over-strictness tradeoff; verify it is monitored/alerted on (Redis-down should page ops, since it silently widens the AI cost-abuse window) rather than being a silent, unnoticed gap.

title: New-conversation creation requires the caller to actually belong to the given project, not merely have generic project-access entitlement
description: createConversation() calls both assertProjectAccess (entitlement) and assertProjectExistsInOrg (existence-in-caller's-org). assertProjectAccess alone returns true for ANY project id when the caller is an org admin, since the entitlement service answers 'may this user access projects' rather than 'does this specific project exist' — assertProjectExistsInOrg is the layer that actually stops a typo'd or cross-org id.
preconditions: Caller is an org-admin-level user (broad project entitlement)
A real project id belonging to a different organization
steps: As the org-admin user, POST /api/assistant/conversations with { projectId: <other-org's real project id> }
expectedResult: Request is rejected 403 'The selected project was not found in your organization' — org-admin entitlement breadth does not bypass the org-boundary existence check.
